newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Slavneft plans hydrocracker, less mazut.
newsitem.headline: Russian Slavneft plans hydrocracker, less mazut.

text.p: Russian-Belarussian joint venture Slavneft said on Wednesday that it had renewed talks to finance a hydrocracking facility at its oil refinery in Belarus, and that heavy fuel oil output would fall as a result.

Fyodor Lisovich, deputy director of the company's developments department, said by telephone from the refinery in Mozyr that talks were underway with unspecified creditors for $480 million in financing.

Slavneft Vice-President Dmitry Romanov, quoted by Interfax news agency late on Tuesday, said the company was seeking a way around troubled relations between Belarus and international lending organisations in order to finance the project.
Lisovich said the technology would come from UOP Limited of the United States and would more than halve fuel oil output while doubling production of products like high-octane gasoline.
Mozyr can process 320,000 barrels per day (bpd), or 16 million tonnes a year, but it is working at about one third of capacity.
It processed 5.7 million tonnes (114,000 bpd) in 1995, according to a 1996 report from Interfax news agency.
Belarus and the Mozyr refinery depend on Russia for crude oil and other energy supplies.

Slavneft, a vertically-integrated oil company, said last year that it planned an issue of American Depositary Receipts and that it would invest $300 million to upgrade Mozyr, of which $60 million had already been guaranteed by the United States Eximbank and $200 million by Japan's Eximbank.
Slavneft also has two refineries in Russia's Yaroslavl.
Slavneft, about 80 percent owned by the Russian government, owns about a 43 percent stake in Mozyr.
The oil company's main production unit is Megionneftegaz.
